correctness.rationale: The factor-occurrence rectangle lemma is an exact equivalence for all nonnegative four gaps, including zero-length gaps. Every possible minimal absent word is classified by its count of one-symbols, 0 through 4; for each class necessity and sufficiency are established via maximal proper prefix/suffix membership, not numerical extrapolation. The uniform K+13 bound reduces the extremal assertion to sums of the three smaller gaps at most 10. On each infinite ray with one gap greater than every other gap by at least 2, all finite candidate tests stabilize and the remaining central family has affine slope at most one. The included standalone verifier checks all 3432 base cases and the two sole affine equality anchors; it separately matches a full factor-set algorithm on 10626 words. Computation alone is not claimed as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimal absent factors encode negative substring information and appear in bioinformatics and anti-dictionary/string-comparison methods. The fixed content of exactly three marked positions is a natural sparse model: the theorem is a sharp all-length capacity with a complete labeled extremizer classification, not an isolated example. Its rectangle recipe describes the whole absent-factor set and exposes how exactly three markers constrain each factor type. The result tightens a general 2n bound to n with equality characterization in this model; no downstream application or major general theorem is asserted.
